quizzes.stem: A team lead wants an assistant to prepare a weekly status email from a spreadsheet of task progress notes. The email goes to executives. Which division of work is soundest?

options.a: Claude collects the notes, writes the email and sends it, with spot checks later
options.b: A person writes the email; Claude only corrects spelling and grammar
options.c: Claude drafts and also decides which blockers to escalate to executives
options.d: Claude writes the first version; a person verifies facts and approves sending

explanation.d: Drafting is language-shaped and reviewable, while checking facts and approving the send stay with a person (the worked example's table).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the table keeps "Check every figure in the draft against the source" with a person or a script, and spot checks later come after readers have the email.
explanation.b: Ruled out because Claude "saves the time spent on prose", the main saving, which a person writing everything forgoes.
explanation.c: Ruled out because escalation is "judgment that carries accountability", which stays with a person.

quizzes.stem: Someone asks Claude: "Summarise this report." The result is accurate, but the sales team who asked cannot use it. Which gap in the request most likely caused this?

options.a: It lacked a role line naming Claude an expert summariser
options.b: It never said who would read it or what they must decide with it
options.c: It omitted a word limit, which is why the summary missed the sales angle
options.d: It ran on a tier too small to judge what matters to sales

explanation.b: The description should cover the goal and the context, who reads it and why, and a generic request gets a generic reply.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a role line names no reader or purpose, and the page says to "Add what a colleague new to the job would need".
explanation.c: Ruled out because without the goal "Claude cannot choose between reasonable readings", and a limit is only a constraint on form.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the description is where most of the quality is decided", and a larger tier does not know the readers either.

quizzes.stem: An analyst asks Claude to summarise a regulation for compliance colleagues. The summary cites "subsection 14(b)(ii)" for a retention rule, and the analyst is about to forward it. What is the most appropriate step?

options.a: Look the passage up in the source of record before sending it on
options.b: Ask Claude whether it is confident, and forward the summary if it says yes
options.c: Ask Claude to cite the subsection again in a fresh reply and compare the two
options.d: Forward it with a note that an AI drafted it, so readers can judge

explanation.a: Specific citations are the kind of detail a model can invent, so the claim that would hurt if wrong is checked against the source of record (the checking routine).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the routine says that asking the model how sure it is, or "for its confidence does not verify anything".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the routine says to check "against the source of record, not against the model", and a second reply from the same model is not the source.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Check in proportion to the cost of being wrong", and a note about an AI draft leaves the unchecked claim in place.

quizzes.stem: A competitor table has one cell marked "data unavailable" while every other cell is filled. A colleague asks you to drop that row so the table looks finished. Which response is best?

options.a: Ask Claude to try again until every cell holds a value
options.b: Fill it with a typical industry figure and label it an estimate
options.c: Retain the entry as it stands and state what could not be located
options.d: Show a dash in that cell and drop any mention of the missing data

explanation.c: A declared gap is information, and the careful move is to keep it and decide what to do (the spotting a gap section).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Regenerating the same request and hoping is the reflex", and pressing for a value invites invention.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the careless move is to fill the gap with an estimate".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "Keep the gap and decide what to do about it", not hide it behind a dash.

quizzes.stem: A team lead wants to hand a monthly board pack entirely to Claude. Which first move reflects sound delegation?

options.a: Give Claude the whole pack once it passes a single test run
options.b: List the steps and keep judgment and figure-checking with people
options.c: Give it only the narrative sections and send them without review
options.d: Hand over everything but ask it to flag anything it is unsure of

explanation.b: Sorting steps into judgment and automatable work is the delegating skill (page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A good draft does not show the figures were right".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the table keeps "Check every figure in the draft against the source" with a person or a script, and review is skipped here.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Claude can state a figure that was never supplied", and a flag raised by the same model is not an independent check.

quizzes.stem: A marketing assistant tells Claude to "make it better" and gets a full rewrite in an unwanted voice. What is the most useful next step?

options.a: Ask again with the same wording and pick the best of the replies
options.b: Move to the highest tier, which follows loose instructions better
options.c: Accept the rewrite and edit it by hand to the voice wanted
options.d: Name the audience, the register to aim for and what to keep, then compare

explanation.d: Describing the audience, the style and what to keep, then comparing, is the iterate-not-re-roll method.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Regenerating the same request and hoping is the reflex", and an identical request is a second guess.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the description is where most of the quality is decided", not the tier.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says "When an output is wrong, ask why before asking again", and hand-editing accepts the rewrite without finding the gap in the request.

quizzes.stem: A manager must explain Claude's role in a new reporting process to colleagues. Which message is most accurate?

options.a: It produces the report end to end, with a spot check each quarter
options.b: It is too unreliable for reports, so it should only reformat finished text
options.c: It speeds up drafting and summaries, while people verify figures and decide
options.d: It drafts, and it also ranks which findings matter to the board

explanation.c: The fair message has three parts: what it speeds up, what still needs a person, and how you will know it works.
explanation.a: Ruled out because it hands the verification away, the first extreme the page names: "it will do the job".
explanation.b: Ruled out because it is the opposite extreme: "it cannot be trusted".
explanation.d: Ruled out because deciding which findings matter is "Decide which variances matter to the board", a step the table gives to a person.

quizzes.stem: A compliance officer must decide how much review an AI-assisted email to a regulator needs. What should that depend on mainly?

options.a: What a wrong claim in it would cost if acted on
options.b: How polished the draft reads after one editing pass
options.c: Which model tier drafted it, since larger tiers need less review
options.d: Whether the draft came with supporting quotes attached

explanation.a: Check in proportion to the cost of being wrong (the checking routine).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Readers check tone and grammar, which are visible", and the damage is in figures and citations.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the routine says "Do not check everything equally", and names no tier that makes verification unnecessary.
explanation.d: Ruled out because supporting quotes make checking faster: "These make checking faster; they do not replace it".
